verses.text: On that day the book of Moses was read aloud to the people. They found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever be allowed into God's assembly,
because they did not meet the Israelites with food and water. Instead they paid Balaam to curse them, but our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard this law, they separated from Israel everyone of foreign descent.
Before this, Eliashib the priest had been put in charge of the storerooms of the temple of our God. He was a relative of Tobiah,

and he had given Tobiah a large room. That room had been used to store the grain offerings, the incense, the temple things, and the tenths of grain, new wine, and olive oil that the law said belonged to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the gifts for the priests.
While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem. In the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, I had gone back to the king. Some time later I asked the king for permission to leave,
and I came back to Jerusalem. Then I found out about the evil thing Eliashib had done for Tobiah by giving him a room in the courtyards of God's temple.
I was very upset, and I threw all of Tobiah's things out of the room.
I gave orders to clean the rooms, and then I put back the things from God's temple, with the grain offerings and the incense.
I also found out that the Levites had not been given their shares of food. So the Levites and singers who did the work had all gone back to their own fields.
So I scolded the officials and asked them, "Why has God's temple been neglected?" Then I called the Levites back and put them back at their posts.
Then all the people of Judah brought their tenths of grain, new wine, and olive oil to the storerooms.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher, and a Levite named Pedaiah in charge of the storerooms. Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, was their helper. These men were known to be honest, and their job was to hand out the shares to their relatives.
Remember me for this, my God. Do not forget the good things I have faithfully done for the temple of my God and its services.

In those days I saw people in Judah pressing grapes on the Sabbath. Others were bringing in bundles of grain and loading them on donkeys, together with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads. They were bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. So I warned them not to sell food on that day.
Some people from Tyre who lived in Jerusalem were bringing in fish and all kinds of goods and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
So I scolded the important men of Judah. I said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing? You are treating the Sabbath day like any other day!
Didn't your ancestors do the same thing? That is why our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city. Now you are making his anger against Israel even worse by not keeping the Sabbath holy."

So when evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and not opened until the Sabbath was over. I put some of my own men at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.
Once or twice, the traders and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
But I warned them, "Why are you spending the night by the wall? If you do this again, I will use force against you." From then on they did not come on the Sabbath.

Then I ordered the Levites to make themselves clean and to go and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this too, my God, and have mercy on me because of your great and faithful love.
In those days I also saw Jewish men who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of some other people, and they could not speak the language of Judah.

I scolded them and called down curses on them. I hit some of them and pulled out their hair. I made them promise in God's name, "You must not let your daughters marry their sons, and you must not take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves.

Wasn't it because of marriages like these that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among all the nations there was no king like him. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel. But even he was led into sin by foreign women.
Should we listen to you and do this terrible evil? Should we be unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat from Horon. So I chased him away from me.
Remember them, my God, because they have made the priesthood unclean and broken the covenant of the priests and Levites.
So I made the priests and Levites clean of everything foreign, and I gave them their duties, each one his own work.
I also arranged for the wood to be brought at set times, and for the first part of the harvest. Remember me kindly, my God.
